info.title: Springtale management API
info.description: Local-first bot automation. Binds loopback; bearer-authenticated.

get.summary: `GET /approvals` — list outstanding approval requests.

post.summary: `POST /approvals/{id}` — land a decision for a pending approval.
post.description:
Status mapping:
- 200: decision recorded, requestor will see it.
- 404: no pending request with that id (timeout already fired, or
  wrong id).
- 409: a prior decision already landed (idempotent — UI shouldn't
  double-click).
- 503: no approval gate wired (test build or boot-incomplete).

post.summary:
POST /auth/login — unauthenticated, rate-limited. Verifies the
passphrase and mints a fresh session token.

POST /auth/logout — drops the presented session. A long-lived token
is not a session; revoke those with `DELETE /auth/tokens/{id}`.

get.summary: GET /auth/tokens — metadata only. The hash never crosses the wire.

post.summary:
POST /auth/tokens — mint a long-lived named token. Authenticated.
The token string is in the response and nowhere else, ever.

delete.summary:
DELETE /auth/tokens/{id} — revoke. The next request carrying that
token fails its lookup, so revocation is immediate.

get.summary: GET /bot/formations — active formations with member info.
GET /bot/memory — list conversation session metadata (zero-knowledge).
get.description:
Per zero-knowledge architecture pattern (Bitwarden, Signal, Matrix):
the server never exposes decrypted conversation content. Memory is
encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 and the decryption key lives in
the bot runtime — not the API layer.

This endpoint returns session metadata only:
- user_id, channel_id (who)
- last_active (when)
- entry_count (how much)

Admin can see what sessions exist and how active they are without
reading message content. This protects vulnerable users' conversations
from API-level data exfiltration, even if the API token is compromised.

Sources:
- Bitwarden: "systems have no knowledge of, way to retrieve" encrypted content
- Matrix Synapse: "encrypted rooms, messages are encrypted, but not their metadata"
- Signal: separates delivery metadata from encrypted contents

get.summary: GET /safety — get the current safety configuration.

post.summary:
POST /safety/disguise/active — focused endpoint that flips just
the disguise-active flag without re-sending the whole config.
Avoids the lost-update race two tabs would hit on the full-config
PUT path.

POST /safety/disguise/profile — atomic two-field update of which
disguise the app should display. Doesn't touch `disguise_active`.
POST /safety/panic-wipe — irreversibly destroy every row of local data.
post.description:
Plan 2.1: the desktop used to reach `operations::safety::panic_wipe`
through its own in-process runtime. The daemon owns the store now, so
the route has to exist here or the button is dead on both shells.

post.summary:
POST /safety/panic_tap_count — update how many rapid title-bar
taps trigger panic-wipe. Server-bounded `[0, 10]`; values out of
range return 400 to prevent a survivor accidentally configuring
panic-wipe unreachable.
POST /send — send a message to a channel on a specific connector.

get.summary: GET /sessions — list all active bot sessions.
get.description:
Shows per-user, per-channel conversation state. Useful for
monitoring which automated conversations are in progress.

get.summary: GET /stream — Server-Sent Events, multiplexed. Ticket auth. Read-only.

200.description: text/event-stream of events, canvas and cooperation frames

post.summary:
POST /stream/ticket — one-time, 30 s ticket for the SSE routes,
issued *against the presented session* (plan 6.6 step 4). The ticket
carries the bearer's principal, so logging out or revoking the token
kills every outstanding ticket with it.
POST /travel/prepare — write an encrypted backup, then wipe local data.
post.description:
Per `ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.6 border-crossing mode. The caller is expected
to stop the daemon afterwards; unlike the old desktop command this does
not call `std::process::exit`, because the daemon may be serving other
clients and killing it out from under them is the wrong shutdown path.

post.summary: POST /travel/restore — decrypt a backup back into vault, database, config.
post.description:
The daemon must be restarted afterwards: it is still holding the handles
to the files that were just replaced underneath it.

parameters.name: path

post.summary: POST /webhook/{connector}/{trigger} — receive an inbound webhook.
post.description:
The management API receives webhook POSTs from external services (GitHub, Kick, etc.)
and routes them to the appropriate connector for signature verification and dispatch.

Flow:
1. Look up connector in registry
2. Connector-specific signature verification (GitHub: HMAC-SHA256, Kick: RSA)
3. Dispatch trigger event to the rule engine via the trigger channel

get.summary: GET /workspaces?formation_id=..&connector=.. — directory listing.

post.summary:
POST /workspaces — manual-entry escape hatch. `entered_by` is a
fresh `AgentId` until Phase 3 auth, same as the desktop command.

POST /workspaces/onboard?ticket=.. — SSE of `chat-discovered`
frames (same payload as the desktop `ChatDiscovered` event) until
the first match, the 60 s window, or client disconnect.
POST /workspaces/onboard-url — resolve the connector's deep link.
POST /workspaces/scan — active `discover_destinations` sweep.

AddAuthorRequest.description: Request body for adding a trusted author.

pubkey.description: Hex-encoded Ed25519 public key (64 hex chars).

target.description: Which level the config applies to (colony, formation, or agent).

AiTarget.description:
One level of the AI command hierarchy. One config key per level:
`ai:colony`, `ai:formation:{formation_id}`, `ai:agent:{rule_id}`.

ai_configured.description: Whether the AI adapter step ran.

connectors_configured.description: Connector names whose config was upserted.

summary.description: Plain-language summary rendered to the user post-deploy.

BotPersona.description:
Bot persona — display name, tone hint, command prefix.

Moved here from `springtale-bot` (plan 6.3): the bot depends on the
runtime, not the reverse, so the settings type the runtime owns and
hands out has to live on this side of the dependency edge.

auto_lock_secs.description:
Idle seconds before the daemon locks itself: drops the runtime,
closes the database and zeroizes the vault key (plan 6.10).
`0` disables auto-lock. Default: 300.

Moved here from `springtale_bot::BotConfig::vault_timeout_secs`,
which nothing read and which could only be changed by editing a
TOML file and restarting — exactly what the product model
forbids of a setting.

session_absolute_secs.description:
Management-API session absolute lifetime, seconds. A session is
dropped this long after login however active it is, so a stolen
token has a bounded life. Default 43200 (12 h).

session_idle_secs.description:
Management-API session idle timeout, seconds. A session with no
accepted request inside this window is dropped. Default 1800.

tool_policy.description:
Which connector actions the AI may call as tools. Default: empty
allow-list — the same default-mode posture as before (read-only
actions only; see `springtale_ai::ToolPolicy`).

CompactMemoryRequest.description:
Request body for compacting memory.

`max_entries` is required: a silent default would quietly delete a
different amount of history than the caller intended.

ConnectorActionStep.description: One step in a W6 action chain.

config.description:
JSON value template — placeholders substituted before passing
to [`crate::operations::config::upsert_connector_config`].

CreateConnectorRuleRequest.description:
Request to create a connector-event rule with simple fields.

Frontend sends field names, backend assembles the full Rule struct.
Eliminates hardcoded "ConnectorEvent"/"RunConnector" type tags in frontend.

Intentionally has no `specta::Type` derive: this struct transitively
references the recursive `Condition` enum (in `conditions`), and per
the rule-module specta policy (see `springtale_core::rule::types`
module doc), rule-shaped types stay schemars-only. The Tauri
command takes `serde_json::Value` and deserializes into this struct
internally — the frontend learns the shape from `get_rule_schema()`.

extra_actions.description:
W6 chain composer — additional action steps run in order after the
primary action. When non-empty, the rule's actions become a single
`Action::Chain` of `[primary, ...extra]`.

match_any.description:
W6 all-of / any-of toggle. `false` (default) = every condition must
hold (the engine's implicit AND over the flat list). `true` = any one
suffices: the conditions are wrapped in a single `Condition::Or`.

CreateFormationRequest.description:
Request body for creating a formation.

Every field is required. An intent that silently defaults to
`Reconnoiter` is a formation whose posture nobody chose.

connectors.description: Connector names the formation's members live on.

DataExport.description:
Exported data snapshot.

`Serialize + Deserialize` so the same type is both the export format and
the import contract — per rust-conventions, serde on data types that
cross boundaries (API, storage) is explicitly allowed.

No `specta::Type` derive — `DataExport` transitively contains
`Rule` (recursive). The Tauri `export_data` command converts to
`serde_json::Value` before crossing the wire, so specta never
sees this type.

oneOf.description:
Geocode a free-text place (the value of `source_input_id`, e.g.
`"city"`) into a `"latitude=..&longitude=.."` query fragment
stored under `target_input_id` (e.g. `"location"`), via the
keyless Open-Meteo geocoding API. Lets the weather strategy take
any city instead of a hardcoded dropdown.

DerivedInputResolver.description:
How a derived input is resolved at deploy time. Internally-tagged so
the JSON wire matches the TS discriminated-union shape, like
[`FieldKind`]. The extension point for the universal-recipe
mechanism — new resolvers (timezone, currency, …) add variants here.

DisguiseActiveBody.description: G5d — request body for toggling disguise-active.

DisguiseProfileBody.description: G5d — request body for switching the disguise profile.

DriftClass.description:
Per-signal verdict. Each signal can independently land on any
of these; the aggregate `DriftReport.overall` is the worst of
the three.

bot_id.description:
Filter to one bot's runs. Both this and `formation_id`
can be set — they intersect.

rule_id.description: Filter to one rule's runs. Required for `rule_drift`.

DriftReport.description: Aggregate drift signal for a recipe / rule.

baseline_runs.description: How many baseline runs informed the analysis.

latency.description: Latency drift — median + p95 duration_ms delta.

overall.description: Overall verdict — the worst-of the three signals.

recent_runs.description: How many recent runs informed the analysis.

refusal_rate.description:
Refusal-rate drift (fraction of `extract` steps with
`schema_invalid` / `refused` errors).

EventListParams.description: Query parameters for a page of the event log.

ExecutionFilterIpc.description:
Mirror of [`ExecutionFilter`] for IPC. Flat, derives `Type`
(the store filter doesn't because it's not crossing the boundary).

status.description: One of the status enum strings — `succeeded | failed | ...`.

ExecutionInfo.description:
IPC-shaped projection of [`ExecutionSummary`]. Flat strings —
no recursion — per `feedback_specta_recursive_types`. Tauri
commands return `Vec<ExecutionInfo>`; the web dashboard reads
the JSON form of the same shape.

mode.description: `cron | webhook | connector_event | file_watch | manual | cooperation | retry | dry_run`.

momentum.description: `cold | warming | hot | fever` — None when momentum unknown.

ExecutionStepInfo.description:
IPC-shaped projection of [`ExecutionStepRow`]. Flat. Sizes-only —
content blob refs forwarded as opaque strings for Phase C.

oneOf.description: Free-form text (no secrecy).

Sensitive value — frontend renders as password input + stores
through the vault rather than plain config.
Numeric input.
Boolean toggle.
URL (validated to scheme http/https).
Picked from a fixed list of options.

Cron expression (5- or 6-field). Frontend renders a
`CronFrequencyChip` next to the input that shows:

  - red 🔴 on sub-minute schedules (preflight blocking)
  - yellow 🟡 on 1–4 minute polls (preflight warning)
  - green 🟢 on ≥5 minute cadences (preflight verified)

Plus a "next 5 fire times" preview computed against the
`cron` crate. Surfaces the same classification the backend's
`check_schedule_frequency` produces so frontend never invents
its own thresholds (per `feedback_zero_frontend_logic`).

CSS selector. Frontend opens the Tauri webview selector picker
at the recipe's target URL — hover-highlights elements,
generates `:nth-of-type` selectors, posts back. Phase B
activates the picker; for now the field renders as text input
with a "test against URL" probe button.

sample_url.description:
Recipe input id whose value the selector picker should
load when launched. E.g. `"watch_url"`. Optional — when
`None`, the picker prompts for the URL inline.

oneOf.description:
JSON Schema for the AI-driven extraction step. Frontend
renders a Monaco-style schema editor (Phase B); falls back to
a textarea today. Schema posts as `serde_json::Value` since
it carries arbitrary user-defined fields.

example.description:
Optional example payload the editor shows alongside the
schema. Recipe authors use this to convey "extract this
shape from a page that looks like X."

oneOf.description:
D1 — external workspace target (messaging chat / channel /
group / user). Renders as a dropdown over the formation's
`mental_model_workspaces` filtered by `connector`, plus a
🔍 Scan button (active discovery via the connector's
`discover_destinations` action), a 🎯 Onboard button
(Telegram-specific deep-link affordance), and an
✏️ Manual entry escape hatch. At deploy time the field
resolves to the raw destination id parsed off the chosen
`WorkspaceKey` URI — recipe TOML stays string-for-string
compatible with the existing `${chat_id}` / `${to}`
substitution. See `docs/intended-arch/COOPERATION.md §21`
(Shared Mental Model — Directory Facilitator extension).

connector.description:
Connector this destination belongs to. e.g.
`"connector-telegram"`.

kinds.description:
Optional `kind` filter — `["channel"]` excludes user DMs,
`["user", "group"]` excludes channels. Empty / unset =
no filter (show everything for this connector).

FieldKind.description:
Internally-tagged so the JSON wire matches the TS discriminated-union
shape `{ kind: "text" } | { kind: "select", options: [...] }`. Unit
variants serialize as `{ "kind": "text" }`, struct variants flatten
the fields next to the tag. Without this serde defaults to external
tagging, which puts unit variants on the wire as bare strings and
breaks the frontend type contract for input rendering.

FieldVisibility.description:
Where an [`InputField`] surfaces in the progressive-disclosure
deploy form, and whether the user is asked at all.

Authors declare this explicitly per field. The frontend renders
each tier behind a chevron (Apple print-dialog "Show Details"
pattern) so a click-and-play user can deploy after touching only
`Required` fields, while a power user can drill into `Optional`
→ `Advanced` on the same surface.

FixGuide.description: Static guidance for a single error ID.

FixOutcome.description: Result of an attempted automated fix.

enabled.description: Whether the monitor is currently ticking.

IncomingMessage.description: A message arriving from an in-app chat panel.

session.description: Optional session id; defaults to the single local in-app session.

InputField.description:
A typed input field the user fills (or that has a default the
recipe author baked in).

default.description:
Default value rendered as the field's initial value. `None`
means the field is empty until the user types.

visibility.description:
Author-declared visibility. Drives progressive-disclosure
layering (Required → Optional → Advanced) and the
recipe-authoring flow (`Baked` fields never show as user
inputs — they ship the recipe's default unchanged).

Per industry research (IFTTT applets, Zapier Zap templates,
GitHub Actions input metadata), this field is **author-declared
per field**, never inferred. No `auto_classify` heuristic.

passphrase.description: The vault passphrase. Verified, never stored, zeroized here.

OnboardBody.description:
Body for both onboarding routes. `config` is the not-yet-deployed
connector config from the deploy form (bot token etc.) — it
travels in the body, never the URL.

PanicTapCountBody.description: G5d — request body for the panic-tap threshold.

oneOf.description:
User needs to fill in a recipe input — frontend should scroll
the matching field into view + focus.
User needs to configure an AI provider (no AI:global yet).
Connector isn't loaded and needs setup before deploy.
Generic message — show as plain text, no action.

PreflightFix.description:
What the frontend should offer to resolve a failing check.
`kind` is a stable enum so the UI maps to the right panel.

PreflightItem.description: One row in the preflight report.

detail.description:
Why the row failed when `status` is `Blocking` or `Warning`,
or extra confirmation text when `Verified`. Plain text.

oneOf.description:
Optional "fix this" hint — server-side recommendation
rendered as an inline action. Frontend may turn it into a
button (e.g. "Configure AI" → opens AiConfigPanel).

id.description:
Stable id for the row (`"secret_present:bot_token"`,
`"connector_loaded:connector-telegram"`). Frontends can
deduplicate / scroll-to-item by this.

label.description: Human-readable label rendered to the survivor (one line).

PreflightReport.description:
Full preflight report — the response body for the `preflight_recipe`
command / `/recipes/{id}/preflight` route.

deployable.description:
Convenience aggregate the frontend uses to enable/disable the
Deploy button without iterating through items itself.

has_warnings.description:
`true` when at least one item is `Warning` and none are
`Blocking` — frontend prompts the user for confirmation
before allowing Deploy.

PreflightStatus.description: Severity tier for an individual preflight check.

errors.description:
Errors encountered during preview (parse failure, missing
placeholder, etc.). Empty when `passed`.

passed.description:
`false` when at least one rule failed to parse or evaluate.
The frontend uses this to gate the recipe-authoring "Clear
Check" (W2.B); deploy form just renders the steps regardless.

PreviewStep.description: One step in the comic-strip narrative.

narrative.description: Plain-language description of what happens at this step.

speaker.description: Who is "speaking" (rule name, connector name, or "system").

would_send_to.description:
What target (chat id, file path, etc.) the bot would have
dispatched to. `None` when the step is informational.

PurgeBody.description:
Body of `POST /data/purge`. Purge destroys every rule, connector,
event, session, and memory row in the store, so the confirmation is
part of the wire format: a stray POST with no body cannot wipe it.

confirm.description: Must be `true`. Anything else is a 400.

ai_required.description:
`true` if the recipe needs a working AI adapter to operate
meaningfully. Surfaces in the card so users running NoopAdapter
can self-filter.

blueprint.description: What `apply_recipe` actually does once the inputs are filled.

icon_id.description: Sprite id rendered by the frontend (`@springtale/ui` sprite map).

id.description:
Stable identifier (kebab-case). Built-ins use literal slugs
(`"telegram-echo"`); user recipes use UUIDs.

inputs.description:
Author-declared input fields. Each carries its own
`FieldVisibility` (Required / Optional / Advanced / Baked) so
the progressive-disclosure UI renders the right tier and
preflight blocks deploy on missing Required values. Order is
the author's preferred render order — frontend does not
re-sort by visibility.

RecipeBlueprint.description:
Blueprint — what `apply_recipe` performs against the running
runtime. All strings may contain `${input_id}` placeholders which
[`crate::operations::recipes::apply`] substitutes from user inputs.

oneOf.description:
AI adapter config to apply, scoped to the colony, an agent,
or a formation.

connector_configs.description: Connector configs to upsert (keyed by connector name).

derived_inputs.description:
Derived inputs resolved at deploy time, BEFORE placeholder
substitution. This is what makes a recipe a universal
"playbook strategy": the commander supplies a free-text target
(e.g. a city), and a resolver turns it into the concrete value
the blueprint needs (e.g. `latitude=..&longitude=..`). Each
resolver's `target_input_id` is treated as a declared
placeholder by `apply`, so the rule TOML can reference it.

summary.description:
Plain-language "what this will do" summary rendered in the
quick-view. Backend-authored so it stays accurate as recipes
evolve (vs. relying on the frontend to compose a summary).

RecipeFilter.description:
Filter passed to [`crate::operations::recipes::library::list_recipes`].

All filtering happens server-side. Frontend sends the filter, gets
the matching slice back — never holds the full catalogue and never
filters in-memory.

oneOf.description: Restrict to a single category. `None` = all.

limit.description: Maximum results to return (server caps at 100 even if larger).

sources.description:
Source filter: `["builtin"]`, `["user"]`, `["community"]`, or any
combination. Empty = all sources.

RecipeInputs.description: What the user submitted when picking a recipe.

RecipePiece.description: One slot the caller can borrow from a recipe.

id.description:
`"trigger:0"`, `"connector_config:1"`, etc. — stable id the
frontend uses as a list key + to request the full piece.

label.description: One-line label rendered in the picker dropdown.

oneOf.description: Compiled into the binary.
Saved by the local user via W2.B authoring flow.

Reserved for the future community marketplace; carries author
identity + Ed25519 signature so the sentinel can verify before
install (W3.A; wire-shape only today).

Report.description: Aggregated result of running all diagnostics.

ResolveDecision.description: The decision a caller landed on a pending request.

ResolveRequest.description: Request body for resolving one pending approval.

toml.description: TOML rule body — placeholders substituted before parse.

SendOutcome.description:
Outcome returned to the caller — connector-friendly message string
and whatever structured output the connector produced.

SendRequest.description: Request to send a message through a specific connector.

channel_id.description: Destination channel/chat id as the connector understands it.

SetAutonomyRequest.description: Request body for setting an agent's autonomy level.

SetHeartbeatRequest.description: Request body for setting the heartbeat interval.

interval_secs.description: Interval in seconds. `0` stops the monitor.

StepAutonomyRequest.description: Request body for stepping an agent's autonomy up or down.

TeamAgentSlot.description: Single agent slot in a team deploy request.

TeamDeployRequest.description: Request to deploy a complete team — creates rules + formation atomically.

output_json.description:
JSON output rendered as a string so specta can describe it
without recursing into `serde_json::Value` (per
`feedback_specta_recursive_types`).

error.description:
Set when the chain failed. Mirrors the executions-log
`error_kind` taxonomy.

ran.description:
`true` when the dispatcher returned `Ok` and the targeted
step was reached. `false` when the chain failed or
short-circuited before the step.

oneOf.description:
The targeted step's recorded output. Populated only when
`ran == true`. Schema mirrors the dispatcher's
[`StepOutput`].

upstream.description:
Every step the dispatcher recorded en route — useful for
the UI's "see the upstream" disclosure. Steps prior to the
targeted one ran in DryRun mode (read-only arms real,
side-effecting arms stubbed).

backup_path.description: Absolute path of the encrypted backup file.

passphrase.description: Vault passphrase — encrypts (prepare) or decrypts (restore) the backup.

WorkspaceInfo.description:
IPC-shaped projection of [`MentalModelWorkspaceRow`]. Flat,
derives `specta::Type` for the Tauri boundary.

metadata_json.description:
Metadata serialized as a JSON string so specta doesn't
recurse into `serde_json::Value` (per
`feedback_specta_recursive_types`).

provenance_json.description:
Serialized `WorkspaceProvenance` enum. The frontend parses
for the tooltip "discovered by … via …" copy.
